entity-newcomer-after-settlescene-entity-transitions0.75 of 0.75 (major)passContinuing entities use one path. Box (Box.tsx:11-17) and Emphasis (Emphasis.tsx:4-5) both render through Entity. Entity is a motion.div with `layout`, `layoutId`, and `transition={LAYOUT_TRANSITION}`, which is { layout: { duration: LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, ease } } with no delay (constants.ts:9,14; Entity.tsx:16-27). So continuing entities start moving at once and settle after 0.6s. Newcomers use a different path. Appear starts at opacity 0 and animates to 1 with { duration: ENTER_T, delay }, where delay defaults to ENTER_DELAY = 0.7s (Appear.tsx:13-19; constants.ts:13). The delay sits only on the Appear wrapper&#39;s opacity. It is not on Entity&#39;s layout transition, so continuing entities do not start late along with the newcomers. Every child of an Appear stays invisible until the wrapper&#39;s delayed fade begins, so each newcomer&#39;s visible entry starts at 0.7s or later, which is at least the 0.6s layout duration. In the sample, all nine steps share groupKey &#39;scene&#39; (steps/index.ts:6-11), so SampleScene stays mounted and each entity is either continuing or new on a given beat. Every entity with a layoutId or id that is first introduced on beats 2-9 is wrapped in Appear (SampleScene.tsx:62-169): - beat 2: skill, the talk arrow, and the chip - beat 3: tray, card 1 and its link arrow, and morph - beat 4: cards 2-4 and their arrows, with explicit delays of 0.7, 0.82 and 0.94s, all at least 0.6s - beat 5: ghost and depth - beat 6: kit - beat 7: verifyLink, verify, and pass - beat 8: route, modifyDown, modifyIn, and edited - beat 9: frame Only two entities render outside Appear: `you` and the focus Emphasis. Both are authored at beat 1. `you` is on every beat. focusRect returns a rect for beats 1-8 (SampleScene.tsx:17-44, 49, 149-159), so the focus ring continues from beat 1 through beat 8. On beat 1 nothing persists, so the beat-1 delay of 0 cannot start an entry before anything settles (SampleScene.tsx:48). The focused test &#39;exits a departing entity through its exit animation and holds newcomers until others settle&#39; (scene-host.test.tsx:116-127) uses a grouped scene whose &#39;stay&#39; Box moves from x=10 to x=300 (scene-host.test.tsx:69-103). It checks that the newcomer&#39;s Appear wrapper starts at opacity 0, is still below 0.5 at 300ms, and later reaches 1. Separately, fit-scale.test.ts:21-22 asserts ENTER_DELAY &gt;= LAYOUT_T. The timing proof rests on these source constants and the code paths above. Judge A fails the criterion because the focus ring is re-rendered without entry motion when navigating back from beat 9 to beat 8. The cited material does not support reading that as a newcomer. In the authored sequence the focus ring is introduced at beat 1 and continues to beat 8 (SampleScene.tsx:24-40). Beat 8 does not introduce it; backward navigation only restores an entity that already existed on that step. The requirement is about &#39;a step [that] introduces a new entity&#39;, and the guidance does not name backward return of a previously departed entity as a scenario. So Judge A&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs:210 createPresentation inserts the user-supplied title into the registry via JSON.stringify and into a single-quoted JS string in Talk.tsx via escapeTitle. escapeTitle does not escape U+2028/U+2029. Those characters are valid in JS strings since ES2019, so this is low risk. A real problem is the String.replace call: `source.replace(REGISTRY_MARKER, entry)` uses `entry` as the replacement string, and `$&`, `$'` or `$$` inside the title are interpreted as replacement patterns. A title containing `$&` or `$'` would corrupt the registry file, possibly duplicating the marker or large parts of the file.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib.mjs:88 withPreview's onSignal handler runs `preview.stop().finally(() => process.exit(...))`. Registering a SIGINT/SIGTERM listener suppresses Node's default exit. If a second signal arrives during the up-to-3s stop, or stop() hangs, the process only exits after the SIGKILL timer. Separately, the vite preview child is spawned without `detached`, and `stop` only signals the direct node child. The 3s SIGKILL timer is cleared as soon as the child exits, so a failure path can leave a hung process.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/verify.mjs:131 main() catches errors from withPreview/browser and records them as `preview/browser error: ${err.message}`, which drops the stack. A browser launch failure caused by a missing Chromium install is reported only by message. The fail handler also calls `process.exit(1)` inside `fail`, so any later cleanup would be skipped. This is a minor loss of diagnostic context.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:238 The settle loop runs at most 40 polls of 100ms and then captures anyway, which is reported only through an advisory warning. With the infinite-animation presentation this adds up to 4s per step. `--settle` and `--viewport` are parsed with no validation: `--settle abc` gives NaN, so `waitForTimeout(NaN)` throws or misbehaves, and a malformed `--viewport` gives NaN dimensions. So the authored deck introduces the focus Emphasis at beat 1, keeps it through beat 8, and then it exits. It is never introduced partway through the deck. On beat 1 nothing persists yet, so there are no settling entities for it to wait for. The only time it renders without entry motion is when the viewer goes back from beat 9 to beat 8. That restores an entity the step already had; step 8 does not introduce it. The review guidance does not name backward return of a departed entity as a scenario. Canvas applies transform scale(scale) to the fixed canvas inside a frame of designW*scale by designH*scale. Box (Box.tsx:11-17) and Emphasis (Emphasis.tsx:4-5) both render through Entity. Entity is a motion.div with `layout`, `layoutId`, and `transition={LAYOUT_TRANSITION}`, which is { layout: { duration: LAYOUT_T = 0.6s, ease } } with no delay (constants.ts:9,14; Entity.tsx:16-27). So continuing entities start moving at once and settle after 0.6s. Newcomers use a different path. Appear starts at opacity 0 and animates to 1 with { duration: ENTER_T, delay }, where delay defaults to ENTER_DELAY = 0.7s (Appear.tsx:13-19; constants.ts:13). The delay sits only on the Appear wrapper&#39;s opacity. It is not on Entity&#39;s layout transition, so continuing entities do not start late along with the newcomers. Every child of an Appear stays invisible until the wrapper&#39;s delayed fade begins, so each newcomer&#39;s visible entry starts at 0.7s or later, which is at least the 0.6s layout duration. In the sample, all nine steps share groupKey &#39;scene&#39; (steps/index.ts:6-11), so SampleScene stays mounted and each entity is either continuing or new on a given beat. Every entity with a layoutId or id that is first introduced on beats 2-9 is wrapped in Appear (SampleScene.tsx:62-169): - beat 2: skill, the talk arrow, and the chip - beat 3: tray, card 1 and its link arrow, and morph - beat 4: cards 2-4 and their arrows, with explicit delays of 0.7, 0.82 and 0.94s, all at least 0.6s - beat 5: ghost and depth - beat 6: kit - beat 7: verifyLink, verify, and pass - beat 8: route, modifyDown, modifyIn, and edited - beat 9: frame Only two entities render outside Appear: `you` and the focus Emphasis. On beat 1 nothing persists, so the beat-1 delay of 0 cannot start an entry before anything settles (SampleScene.tsx:48). It checks that the newcomer&#39;s Appear wrapper starts at opacity 0, is still below 0.5 at 300ms, and later reaches 1. Separately, fit-scale.test.ts:21-22 asserts ENTER_DELAY &gt;= LAYOUT_T. The timing proof rests on these source constants and the code paths above. Judge A fails the criterion because the focus ring is re-rendered without entry motion when navigating back from beat 9 to beat 8. The cited material does not support reading that as a newcomer. In the authored sequence the focus ring is introduced at beat 1 and continues to beat 8 (SampleScene.tsx:24-40). Beat 8 does not introduce it; backward navigation only restores an entity that already existed on that step. The requirement is about &#39;a step [that] introduces a new entity&#39;, and the guidance does not name backward return of a previously departed entity as a scenario. I did that: node text 14→18 px, card and chip text 11–12→15–17 px, icons 22 px, and small chips were widened to fit. Effective size at 390 px is now about 6–7 px, up from about 4–5 px. A regression unit test (`tests/unit/sample-legibility.test.mjs`) pins a minimum design size for the sample's diagram text. Caption, title and chrome were already legible and are unchanged."},{"line":1217,"text":"- Rationale: Making diagram text fully phone-readable would need something the approved definition rules out or leaves open: reflowing or re-laying-out the diagram for narrow widths (contradicts \"without reflowing its internal composition\"), or a different canvas for the sample, which the spec permits only as a presentation-level override and which would redesign the nine-step sample.
